editorial.thesis: A motor-trade-and-learning city of about 3.9 million. Its retail is heavy on coaching & training and cafés, tea & coffee, and thin on apparel, footwear & jewellery and desserts, sweets & ice cream — and 9% of residents live in zones with under 60% of the city's average retail depth.
takeaways: Branded retail is level with Mumbai. 24.61 chain outlets per lakh residents against 23.76 in Mumbai; 47 of the 51 national brands we track are present, led by Café Coffee Day 93, Domino's 77, MedPlus 61.

The mapped economy leans to automotive. Shares of all mapped places: automotive 3.1% (Mumbai 2.2%); malls & department stores 0.5% (Mumbai 0.4%); other services 7.3% (Mumbai 8.4%); desserts & sweets 1.0% (Mumbai 1.1%). Raw counts would mislead because Mumbai is mapped more completely (70,423 places against 58,716), so we compare mix, not counts.
Supply and demand are misaligned. 2 zones hold 9% of residents with under 60% of the city's average retail depth. Katraj alone has about 180,000 residents and 182 mapped food & drink places.
Retail is more concentrated than in Mumbai. 44% of commercial places sit in the busiest tenth of the city (Mumbai 38%). The largest cores are Vadgaon Sheri (3,309 places) and Sachapir Street (2,987).

The widest brand gaps against Mumbai. Café Coffee Day 93 outlets vs 169; Starbucks 20 outlets vs 64; Domino's 77 outlets vs 115. These are leads to check against live listings, not verdicts: a brand may trade under another name or have opened since the map was updated.

numbers.title: The city in eight numbers
numbers.deck: A 10 km circle around the centre, processed with the same rules as Mumbai, so every comparison is like for like. Where raw counts would mislead — because a bigger city is mapped more completely — we compare shares and mix instead.

map.title: Where people live, where shops are
map.deck: Switch layers. The amber “gap” layer is the one to study: it marks places with many residents but little retail around them. Hover any hexagon (about 0.1 km²) for its numbers; click a zone on the right to isolate it.

captions.residents: Where people live. Sachapir Street and Vadgaon Sheri are the largest zones by residents (280,000 and 266,000). Modelled residents per square kilometre.
captions.supply: Where the shops are. The busiest tenth of cells hold 44% of all commercial places, and Vadgaon Sheri alone lists 3,309.
captions.chains: Where the brands are. Vadgaon Sheri holds 101 of the 955 tracked chain outlets, and Sachapir Street adds 77.
captions.education: Where the campuses are. Vadgaon Sheri and Kothrud · Ex. Serviceman Colony lead on education places (320 and 306, with 137 and 142 coaching centres) — a daytime youth market that residents alone do not show.
captions.gap: The gap. Amber: many residents nearby, little retail. Blue: far more retail than local residents explain — the commercial cores that draw people in. The deepest amber sits in Katraj and Armament. The blue cores include Vadgaon Sheri.

zones.title: Zone by zone, by PIN code
zones.deck: Each zone is a postal-code area. Residents are modelled counts; places are mapped businesses and services. “Retail depth” is places per 10,000 residents — the tick marks the city average. Click a row to see it on the map.

mix.title: What the retail layer is made of
mix.deck: Raw counts per resident would favour whichever city is mapped more completely (70,423 places in Mumbai against 58,716 here). So this compares each category's share of all mapped places. 100 means the same share as Mumbai; below 100 is thinner, above is stronger.
mix.note: Against Mumbai, Pune's mapped places over-index on automotive (3.1% vs 2.2%), malls & department stores (0.5% vs 0.4%), education (9.4% vs 7.5%) and under-index on other services (7.3% vs 8.4%), desserts & sweets (1.0% vs 1.1%), banks & finance (7.1% vs 7.8%).

chains.title: Who is mapped here, and who is not
chains.deck: 955 outlets of 47 tracked national brands within 10 km — 24.61 per lakh residents against Mumbai's 23.76 (1266 outlets of 44 brands). Filled names have at least one mapped outlet (count shown); dashed names have none.
chains.note: Read dashed names as leads, not verdicts. “No mapped outlet” can mean a brand trades under a different listed name, or has opened since the map was updated. The widest gaps against Mumbai are Café Coffee Day (93 vs 169); Starbucks (20 vs 64); Domino's (77 vs 115). Premium reports check every lead against live listings.

formats.title: Which formats have room
formats.deck: 9 formats, thinnest first. The index is the format's share of all mapped places relative to Mumbai's, so low means thin by Mumbai's standard. “Where to look” ranks zones with at least 40,000 residents by residents per mapped outlet — a first-pass screen for where one more outlet would face the least local competition.

people.title: Who the customers are
people.deck: Age mix inside the 10 km circle, from Meta's age rasters (modelled, not a census).
people.note: Pune's age mix against Mumbai: children (0–14) 24.4% vs 19.9%, 15–24 19.7% vs 19.7%, working age 46.8% vs 52.0%, 60+ 9.1% vs 8.4%. Under-25s are 44% of residents.

restaurants.read: Restaurants & fast food are 7.5% of mapped places against 7.0% in Mumbai, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Domino's 77 (Mumbai 115), Pizza Hut 54 (Mumbai 53), Subway 50 (Mumbai 81), McDonald's 48 (Mumbai 73).
restaurants.watch: Independent eateries are numerous and unevenly mapped. Treat the index as a screen and confirm competitor density street by street.

cafes.read: Cafés, tea & coffee are 3.2% of mapped places against 2.7% in Mumbai — above its share. Mapped chain outlets: Café Coffee Day 93 (Mumbai 169), Starbucks 20 (Mumbai 64), Blue Tokai 12 (Mumbai 25), Third Wave Coffee 12 (Mumbai 16).
cafes.watch: Chai stalls and independent cafés are under-mapped. A café concept here competes on price and habit as much as on novelty.

desserts.read: Desserts, sweets & ice cream are 1.0% of mapped places against 1.1% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Baskin Robbins 31 (Mumbai 57), Naturals 9 (Mumbai 18), Theobroma 3 (Mumbai 22), Havmor 2 (Mumbai 11).
desserts.watch: Traditional sweet shops are the real benchmark and sit outside most chain lists.

grocery.read: Grocery & daily needs are 1.8% of mapped places against 1.9% in Mumbai, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: Reliance Smart / Fresh 24 (Mumbai 18), DMart 15 (Mumbai 24), Big Bazaar 7 (Mumbai 8), Star Bazaar 7 (Mumbai 4). No mapped outlet in either city: Easyday.
grocery.watch: Neighbourhood kirana stores are the real incumbents and the least completely mapped outlets, so any gap is overstated. Test a site against local store density before acting.

pharmacy.read: Pharmacy & health retail are 1.3% of mapped places against 1.3% in Mumbai, so the mix is level. Mapped chain outlets: MedPlus 61 (Mumbai 1), Apollo Pharmacy 50 (Mumbai 45), Wellness Forever 12 (Mumbai 17). No mapped outlet in either city: Frank Ross.
pharmacy.watch: Independent chemists are dense and lightly mapped. Hospital and clinic clusters are the natural anchors.

apparel.read: Apparel, footwear & jewellery are 4.1% of mapped places against 4.8% in Mumbai — below its share. Mapped chain outlets: Bata 44 (Mumbai 52), Titan 41 (Mumbai 32), Reliance Trends 28 (Mumbai 20), Tanishq 25 (Mumbai 32).
apparel.watch: Established multi-brand traders and local bazaars sit behind these numbers; new entrants compete with them as well as with chains.

banking.read: Banks & ATMs are 7.1% of mapped places against 7.8% in Mumbai, so the mix is level.
banking.watch: This category includes insurance and agency offices, so it overstates branch banking. Use it as a signal of commercial activity, not a branch count.

coaching.read: Coaching & training are 3.4% of mapped places against 2.7% in Mumbai — above its share.
coaching.watch: Coaching demand follows the exam calendar. Formats that depend on it should be tested across the academic year.

fitness.read: Fitness & wellness are 4.6% of mapped places against 4.4% in Mumbai, so the mix is level.
fitness.watch: Gym listings change often and are inconsistently categorised; verify before drawing conclusions.
